execution: Not executable yet. M0 must bind agreed cases and resolve proposed cases before claiming coverage.

cases.given: A fresh installation has no network.
actions: Create Family A and record a diaper.
Restart the app and export A.
expect: A and its entry remain available without an account or relay.
The export contains the recorded entry.

cases.given: A local Family has existing history.
actions: Choose to share A.
Interrupt connectivity before confirmation.
expect: Local history remains readable and writable.
The UI does not assert that sharing completed without confirmation.
variants: disconnect after relay commit before response

cases.given: A fresh installation holds a valid invitation.
actions: Complete the authorized join flow.
expect: The invited Family is available.
No unwanted empty local Family is created.

cases.given: Alice manages A; Bob is a member.
actions: Bob attempts to remove Alice through the UI and a direct unauthorized request.
expect: Membership does not change.
Bob can still record entries.

cases.given: Alice is the only manager of A.
actions: Alice attempts to remove or demote herself without a successor.
expect: The shared Family is not left without a manager.
The UI explains that another manager is required.

cases.given: Alice is offline and last knew herself to be a manager.
actions: Attempt a membership change.
Record an entry before reconnecting.
expect: The app does not claim the membership change has completed.
The local entry is retained.
open_details: Whether offline membership requests are queued or require retry remains an implementation UX choice to document.

cases.given: Alice and Bob are the only managers of A and each requests removal of the other.
actions: Commit Alice removing Bob first.
Deliver Bob removing Alice next.
Reconnect both clients.
expect: Alice remains the manager of original Family A.
Bob cannot remove Alice using his former authority.
Bob sees access ended and that his removal request did not take effect.
Both retain their respective local histories and pending edits.
Bob's pending work is saved in one automatic private copy after verified removal; Alice may explicitly make her own copy.
variants: exchange Alice and Bob and reverse committed order
deliver a duplicate of each request

cases.given: Both managers are offline and each tries to remove the other.
actions: Record local entries on both devices.
Reconnect and submit both removal attempts.
expect: No access change was represented as confirmed while offline.
The first valid committed removal governs original Family A.
Each device retains its own pending entries regardless of the outcome.
variants: both reconnect before either request commits

cases.given: Both managers requested mutual removal; Alice removal of Bob commits but its response is lost.
actions: Restart Alice device.
Retry or query the action result.
Reconnect Bob.
expect: Alice does not mistake a timeout for proof that removal failed.
The committed removal is discovered without applying a second access change.
Both clients eventually report the same original-Family membership.
variants: restart after remote commit before local persistence

cases.given: Alice and Bob manage A; Charlie is an unaffected member.
actions: Execute either order of mutual manager removal.
Reconnect Charlie.
expect: Charlie remains a member of original Family A.
Charlie is not silently redirected into either private copy.
The surviving manager remains visible when current membership is known.
variants: Charlie is offline during the race

cases.given: Alice requests removal of Bob while Bob requests demotion of Alice; both initially manage A.
actions: Commit one change.
Deliver the other request from the prior membership state.
expect: The first change takes effect.
The second cannot execute using authority the requester no longer has.
Clients explain current role/access rather than claiming both requests succeeded.

cases.given: Alice and Bob are the only managers and request demotion of each other.
actions: Commit one demotion.
Deliver the other request.
expect: One manager remains.
The demoted member cannot complete the competing demotion.
The demoted member retains ordinary read/write access.

cases.given: Bob has local history and pending work when his shared access ends.
actions: Reconnect and learn access has ended.
Let the app create one private copy for the pending work.
Restart and export the new Family.
expect: Existing local records and pending work are preserved according to the event model.
The copy has independent identity and keys and starts local-only.
The app identifies where the pending work was saved and does not make a second copy after restart.
New records in the copy do not sync into the original.
The export is scoped to the copy.

cases.given: Bob learns his access ended and has no pending local work or new action targeted at the removed Family.
actions: Dismiss the notice.
Read and export the locally retained history.
expect: The app does not erase local data or silently create a shared replacement.
No unused private Family is created automatically; the archive and explicit independent-copy option remain distinguishable.

cases.given: Alice remains an authorized manager and holds a local copy.
actions: Explicitly create an independent local Family from that copy.
expect: The copy does not require another manager approval.
It has independent identity and keys.
Creating a copy does not silently change original Family membership.

cases.given: An independent-copy operation is underway with pending local entries.
actions: Interrupt the process and restart.
expect: The source history and pending entries remain recoverable.
A partial copy is not represented as complete.
Retry does not mix source and destination Family identities.
variants: interrupt after destination commit before UI confirmation

cases.given: Bob cannot reach the relay; no removal is confirmed.
actions: Keep recording entries.
Read sharing status.
expect: Entries remain locally available.
The app reports connection/confirmation uncertainty, not an invented removal.
No automatic private Family is created merely because sync is unavailable.
variants: rate limit or storage quota response

cases.given: Charlie remains authorized but was offline while Bob was removed.
actions: Charlie records offline entries.
Reconnect Charlie and refresh shared access.
Upload retained pending work.
expect: Charlie pending work enters shared history exactly once under current authorization.
Bob cannot read the new-key uploads.
The UI does not ask Charlie to re-enter the records.

cases.given: Alice created a valid unused invitation to A with a specified role.
actions: Bob opens the invitation and completes enrollment.
expect: Bob joins and receives history with the specified role without a second manual manager approval.
The invitation is consumed by this enrollment and cannot enroll another device.

cases.given: A remote invitation was canceled or expired before redemption.
actions: Try to join using the old invitation.
expect: No new access is granted.
The UI explains the unusable invitation and offers a fresh invitation route.
An existing unrelated Family on the device is unchanged.
variants: expired seven days after committed creation before redemption
issuer lost manager authority before redemption

cases.given: Alice issued an unused invitation for Charlie; Bob is removing Alice.
actions: Order Charlie enrollment and Alice removal in both ways.
Refresh membership on remaining clients.
expect: Enrollment committed while Alice invitation remained authorized is not silently undone by her later removal.
Alice removal or demotion invalidates her still-unused invitation before any later redemption.
A committed pending enrollment survives later issuer removal or invitation expiry unless a manager separately removes the pending device.
Charlie receives a confirmed joined state or a clear unusable invitation state.
variants: pending device separately removed before activation

cases.given: One app is manager in A and member in B.
actions: Log in B.
Manage membership in A.
Export each Family.
expect: Only B contains the logged entry.
Only A membership changes.
Each export contains only its selected Family.

cases.given: One app participates in A and B and has pending work in both.
actions: Access to A ends.
Reconnect B and choose an independent copy of A.
expect: B remains writable and syncing with its existing identity.
A pending work survives in its independent copy.
No A entries are redirected into B.

cases.given: A timer started for child X in Family A.
actions: Switch the app to child Y in Family B.
Stop the original timer.
expect: The stop targets child X in A.
Family B receives no timer entry as a side effect.

cases.given: A widget or watch still targets A after access to A ended; the phone now displays B.
actions: Attempt quick logging or stop a running timer.
expect: The action keeps its A and child target; after verified removal it is saved once in a private copy of locally held A data.
No entry is silently written into B.
The surface explains changed access and identifies the private destination.
Repeated delivery of the same action does not create another Family or entry.

cases.given: The sole local-only device is lost and no saved record backup exists.
actions: Attempt recovery.
expect: The app does not claim missing records were recovered.
It explains that records held only on the lost device cannot be restored.

cases.given: A Family has a complete readable or password-protected record backup; the protection credential is available if needed.
actions: Lose the original device.
Restore the file on a fresh installation without contacting the original relay.
expect: The saved children, entries, required metadata, units, and unknown fields round-trip according to the full-file contract.
The saved record state includes local pending work present at backup time.
Restore creates a new independent local-only Family with fresh identity and keys.
Original membership and device credentials are not restored.
The UI identifies the backup point; later unsaved records are not invented.
variants: saved unknown fields and event types

cases.given: The only manager lost their only authorized device; ciphertext history remains on the relay.
actions: Try to join the original Family on a fresh installation.
If a complete file backup exists, restore it.
expect: A fresh installation without the old device's private key cannot claim its manager authority or decrypt relay history by account, phrase, or file restore.
If a complete file was saved, it restores only saved records into a new local Family with fresh keys and no original membership.
Without a saved copy, the app does not claim the lost records are recoverable.
variants: old device reconnects with its own still-authorized keys

cases.given: Bob's device is removed from shared Family A; Bob holds an old full file backup and another device may also be enrolled.
actions: Restore the file on a fresh installation.
If Bob has another enrolled device, inspect its separate authorization.
expect: The file restores saved data only into a new Family and cannot reinstate the removed device in A.
An independently enrolled device retains its own A access until that device is explicitly removed.
A display-name match or a paid-service account does not revoke or restore another device.
variants: another device enrolled with a member role
another device enrolled with a manager role

cases.given: The last completed full-file backup predates recent entries, or no backup exists.
actions: Inspect backup status before losing the device.
expect: The app identifies the last completed saved point or says no backup is known.
It does not claim unsaved entries or original-Family authority are recoverable from a file, account, or relay ciphertext alone.

cases.given: A relay withholds the latest history from one client.
actions: Sync that client without any out-of-band history source.
expect: Locally held records remain available.
The test does not demand detection of an unknowable hidden latest entry.
The product does not promise that server sync proves universal history completeness.

cases.given: Bob was removed; relay hides the rotation from Carol, who still knows only the old key.
actions: Carol sends old-key ciphertext to the malicious relay.
Relay gives that ciphertext to Bob.
expect: The scenario records an accepted confidentiality limitation: Bob may decrypt old-key ciphertext.
No product claim treats all wall-clock-later entries as protected.
Separate tests still require Bob to be unable to decrypt new-key ciphertext.

cases.given: Two caregivers edit the same field while offline.
actions: Reconnect in both delivery orders.
Inspect the resulting record and displaced edit.
expect: The resulting state converges according to the event model.
The displaced value can be inspected and explicitly restored.
Restore is a new edit, not deletion of history.

cases.given: Bob continued in an independent local Family after removal.
actions: Share the independent Family later.
Record entries in both the original and independent Families.
expect: Each Family has separate membership and subsequent history.
No automatic reunification or child-history merge occurs.

cases.given: Two different devices possess the same valid unused invitation.
actions: Both attempt enrollment concurrently.
Deliver enrollment requests in either order.
expect: Exactly one enrollment can commit.
The other device receives an already-used result and no access from the consumed invitation.

cases.given: Bob already enrolled using an invitation.
actions: Try the same invitation on a different device.
expect: The used invitation cannot grant another enrollment, even with the same display name.
The second device needs a fresh invitation from an active manager.
variants: same intended caregiver on another device

cases.given: Bob enrollment committed but the response was lost.
actions: Restart or reconnect the joining client.
Resume the original enrollment using its device credentials.
Try resuming from another device holding only the link.
expect: Bob can discover and complete the same enrollment without a second membership record.
Possession of the link alone does not authorize the other device to resume Bob enrollment.

cases.given: An invitation is valid and unused.
actions: Preview the link or scan its QR code without submitting enrollment.
The intended recipient later completes enrollment.
expect: Viewing or previewing does not consume the invitation or disclose Family history.
The recipient can still perform its one authorized enrollment.

cases.given: An unintended recipient obtains a valid unused invitation.
actions: The unintended recipient redeems it before the intended recipient.
The intended recipient subsequently tries to join.
expect: The first recipient can join under the agreed bearer-invitation policy; this is an accepted risk.
The intended recipient sees that the invitation is already used and needs a new invitation.
Removing the unintended recipient cannot retract history already received.

cases.given: Bob has a complete data backup of A but was subsequently removed from shared Family A.
actions: Restore the backup offline.
Record a new entry in restored Family B.
Choose to share B and invite a caregiver.
expect: Saved data is available without original manager permission.
B has fresh identity and keys; its new entry never silently joins A.
Restoring and sharing B do not reinstate Bob membership in A.
Caregivers must join B through new invitations; A membership is not copied.

cases.given: The app already has Families A and C, and a full backup originally exported from A.
actions: Restore the file into a new local Family B.
expect: A and C retain their records, roles, keys, and sync state.
B contains the saved data as a separate Family.
A matching original Family or child identifier in the file does not trigger automatic merge or replacement.
variants: same child display name in C

cases.given: A Family has children, recorded activities, and locally held metadata.
actions: Export readable CSV and a full structured file.
Read both in another program without contacting the relay.
expect: Export does not require a password or enabling encrypted-file mode.
The documented formats support analysis and portability.
The full structured file is restorable; CSV is not presented as a full-fidelity backup.
Neither export includes original shared device credentials or epoch keys.

cases.given: A backup was saved before several later entries were logged; the original device and later records are now unavailable.
actions: Restore the saved backup into a new Family.
expect: The saved records are restored.
The backup point is clear and later missing records are not invented.
Successful restore does not imply that records after the saved snapshot were recovered.

cases.given: Existing local Families are intact and the selected backup cannot be decoded or unlocked.
actions: Attempt file restore.
expect: The app reports restore failure and does not claim records were recovered.
Existing Families remain unchanged.
A failed restore is not presented as a completed empty replacement Family.

cases.given: A complete backup is being restored into a new independent Family.
actions: Interrupt the app at a restore boundary.
Restart and inspect or resume the operation.
expect: Existing Families and the source backup remain intact.
An incomplete destination is not presented as a completed restore.
Resuming the same restore either completes its intended new Family or reports a recoverable failure without mixing identities.
variants: interruption after destination commit before UI confirmation

cases.given: Alice removed Bob and an authorized device with a pinned Family control head is receiving the new epoch grant through a malicious relay.
actions: Replace, omit, or replay that device's grant or keyring ciphertext.
Attempt to log a new entry from the device.
expect: The device rejects an uncommitted, incomplete, wrong-recipient, stale, or mismatched key transcript before encrypting new shared data.
The relay cannot read the device's later-epoch entry or give Bob a usable later-epoch key.

cases.given: Bob has a valid unused invitation but no existing Family device holding the key is online.
actions: Commit Bob's one-device enrollment using the invitation.
Bring an existing authorized key holder online later.
expect: Only Bob's exact device and fixed invited role are enrolled pending key activation; the invitation cannot enroll a second device.
Before verified key delivery and device acknowledgement, Bob sees that he joined but is waiting for history and cannot read, write, or exercise the invited role in the shared Family.
The holder delivers history access automatically without another manual approval, and activation binds Bob's exact device to the then-current Family head and epoch.
A lost response resumes the same pending enrollment or activation rather than consuming another invitation.
variants: holder comes online without an intervening rotation
epoch rotates while Bob is pending
Bob is a pending manager while the only active manager tries to leave
activation response is lost after commit

cases.given: Charlie submitted an old-epoch upload during Bob's removal race and lost the response, so Charlie does not yet know whether it committed before cutover.
actions: Rotate the epoch to remove Bob.
Restart and reconnect Charlie.
Query or pull the stable batch result before rebatching any still-uncommitted operations under the new epoch.
expect: Charlie's operation takes effect once in the original Family, regardless of batch retry or rebatching.
Charlie's local pending work is retained until its committed result is known.
A replacement batch keeps the operation ID but cannot overwrite or impersonate an already committed batch.
variants: restart before the client persists the queried result

cases.given: A local Family has earlier creates, edits, deletions, and pending work.
actions: Share the Family and receive confirmation.
Enroll a second device and read its history.
expect: A staged or incomplete promotion cannot be joined or appear as a confirmed share.
The new device verifies and receives the complete manifested local history through the share watermark, including deletions and preserved unknown data.
Pending work above the watermark remains in the durable outbox and enters shared history exactly once under ordinary sync.
A failed or unknown promotion leaves the local Family usable and never appears as a confirmed complete share.
variants: relay omits or substitutes a manifested chunk
new local operation while promotion is staged

cases.given: Bob is a member and knows the shared epoch key but not Alice's signing key.
actions: Submit an encrypted batch claiming Alice's device ID and next sequence.
Then let Alice submit her genuine pending batch.
expect: Bob's batch is rejected as Alice's work.
Alice's genuine work is not displaced by Bob's forged device identity.
A valid signed batch from another Family, epoch, state, device, or sequence position is not accepted as this batch.
variants: copied ciphertext with a changed envelope

cases.given: Bob opened a valid invitation and the joining devices are not online at the same time.
actions: Let Bob submit enrollment and background or close the joining app.
Later let an authorized key holder sync, including through a supported background wake.
Let Bob's app sync again after the grant is available.
expect: The attempt persists across app suspension and restart; no second human approval or deliberate reopen is needed when background execution is delivered.
The UI identifies whether enrollment is pending, a Family key holder is needed, the grant and history are being verified and loaded, or shared use is ready.
A delayed or unavailable wake leaves an accurate pending state and resumes on the next sync opportunity without claiming a completion deadline.
Bob cannot read, write, or exercise an invited manager role before verified activation.
variants: key holder syncs after Bob goes offline
Bob retrieves the grant after the holder goes offline
background wake delivered to each app

cases.given: Alice uses two installations in Family A and has no global account; each installation was separately invited and has its own role and keys. A fresh third installation has neither device's private keys.
actions: A manager removes Alice's first device.
Use Alice's second device and try to use a fresh installation with the same display name or paid-service account.
expect: Only the first device loses A access at the committed cutover; the second retains its independently granted role.
The fresh installation has no A access until an active manager issues it a new invitation.
A matching label or unrelated account does not grant, combine, or revoke Family device authority.

cases.given: The sole manager device for A is lost; Carol remains an authorized member with locally held A data but cannot manage A.
actions: Carol deliberately starts a new Family B from her local A data.
Carol invites another device into B and stops using A locally.
expect: B has fresh Family and device identities, and Carol is its manager.
B contains only history Carol actually held, including her pending local work; incomplete known sync is disclosed before copying.
Other devices join B only through new invitations; A access and relay history are not remotely revoked or erased by the copy.
Carol can archive or hide A locally without claiming its lost manager credential was revoked.
variants: Carol's A history is fully synced
Carol knows A history is incomplete

cases.given: Bob has a durable local entry for A, but the relay is unreachable and Bob does not know whether an access change occurred.
actions: Keep the entry pending while offline.
Reconnect and verify that Bob's device was removed before that entry could commit.
expect: No removal or private fork is inferred from the outage alone.
Verified removal creates one local-only private copy containing Bob's locally held A data and the uncommitted entry.
Bob sees where the entry was saved; it is not sent to another open Family or accepted into A after removal.
A crash, retry, or repeated notice does not create another private Family or duplicate the entry.
variants: restart after private-copy commit before UI notice
